fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Empty `file_impact` is overloaded (see parent epic): "the author forgot" and "this ticket
touches no repo file" are the same value today, so every consumer must assume the conservative
reading. This story adds the missing third state to the data model and every surface that
writes or reads it. No gate behavior changes here — consumers are wired in S2/S3/S4/S5.

## Approach

Extend the existing `FILE_IMPACT` event rather than adding a new event type, so the
last-writer-wins semantics already implemented in
`process_file_impact` (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:527) make the states inherently
mutually exclusive: a later declaration replaces an earlier one, in one place.

Event payload gains two optional keys alongside `file_impact`:

```json
{"file_impact": [], "file_impact_scope": "none", "no_file_impact_reason": "operator action only: rotates the Gerrit service key in the console; no repo file changes"}
```

Reducer state gains `file_impact_scope` (default `"undeclared"`) and `no_file_impact_reason` (default
`""`). `process_file_impact` sets BOTH on every FILE_IMPACT event, so recording paths after a
`none` declaration resets the state to `"paths"` with an empty reason, and vice versa. The
derivation rule is fixed and single-sourced in one helper:

- non-empty `file_impact` → `"paths"` (any `file_impact_scope` in the payload is ignored);
- empty `file_impact` + `file_impact_scope == "none"` → `"none"`;
- otherwise → `"undeclared"`.

Write surface — CLI keeps ONE verb (`set-file-impact`) with a new mutually-exclusive form:

```
rebar set-file-impact <id> '[{"path":"…","reason":"…"}]'     # unchanged
rebar set-file-impact <id> --none "<reason>"                  # new
```

`--none` requires a reason of at least 10 non-whitespace characters (a bare `--none` or
`--none ""` is a usage error, exit 2) — the reason is what the S4 criterion reviews. Passing
both a JSON array and `--none` is a usage error.

Read surface — `get-file-impact` keeps its array shape (its schema is an array and
`next_batch` consumes it); the tri-state is read through a new
`rebar.get_file_impact_scope(ticket_id) -> {"kind": str, "reason": str, "paths": list}` library
function and is included in `show`/ticket-state output via the reducer state keys.

MCP gets a dedicated write tool `declare_no_file_impact(ticket_id, reason)` rather than
overloading `set_file_impact`'s array parameter, so each tool keeps a single clean
`outputSchema`; `set_file_impact` is unchanged over the wire and still resets the state to
`"paths"`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py` — initial state keys `file_impact_scope` / `no_file_impact_reason`.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — `process_file_impact` sets the tri-state; the
  derivation helper lives here next to the processor that applies it.
- `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py` — `set_file_impact` grows a `no_file_impact_reason` keyword;
  reason-length validation.
- `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_cli/help/set-file-impact.txt` (created if
  absent) — the `--none` argument form and its help text.
- `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` — `set_file_impact` passthrough plus `get_file_impact_scope`.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — export `get_file_impact_scope` and `declare_no_file_impact`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py` — the `declare_no_file_impact` tool.
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json` — the
  `file_impact_scope` enum + `no_file_impact_reason`; `src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py` regeneration
  into `src/rebar/types.py` (`TicketState`).
- `docs/event-schema.md` — the FILE_IMPACT event's new keys.

Out of scope (later children): manifest/attestation behavior, container inheritance, the P9
lint, the new review criterion, the close gate.

## Testing

- Reducer unit tests: each of the six transitions between the three states (including
  paths→none→paths) lands the expected `file_impact_scope` / `no_file_impact_reason` pair.
- CLI tests: `--none "<reason>"` appends the event; `--none` with a short/empty reason exits
  2 with a usage error; array + `--none` together exits 2.
- Schema test: a state carrying `file_impact_scope: "none"` validates against
  `ticket_state.schema.json`, and an unknown `file_impact_scope` value fails validation.
- MCP test: `declare_no_file_impact` round-trips through the reducer state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar set-file-impact <id> --none "<reason ≥10 chars>"` records the declaration, and
      `rebar.get_file_impact_scope(<id>)` returns `{"kind": "none", "reason": <reason>, "paths": []}`
      (checked: CLI + library test).
- [ ] Recording a non-empty JSON array after a `--none` declaration returns the ticket to
      `{"kind": "paths", "reason": ""}` (checked: reducer transition test).
- [ ] A ticket that has never been declared returns `{"kind": "undeclared", …}` and existing
      `get-file-impact` output is byte-identical to before this change (checked: existing
      `get-file-impact` tests pass unmodified).
- [ ] `--none` with a reason under 10 non-whitespace characters exits 2 with a message naming
      the minimum (checked: CLI test asserting exit code and message).
- [ ] The MCP tool `declare_no_file_impact` is listed with an `outputSchema` and sets the same
      state as the CLI (checked: MCP tool test).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full test suite pass.
fields.title: Tri-state file-impact scope: FILE_IMPACT carries an explicit 'no file impact' declaration
